cases.name: Cox and Kings Ltd. v. SAP India Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: A five-Judge Bench considered whether non-signatories could be bound by an arbitration agreement under the group of companies doctrine.
cases.issue: What is the scope of the referral court's enquiry under Section 11 where joinder of a non-signatory is disputed?
cases.ratioDecidendi: At the referral stage the court's enquiry is confined to the existence of the arbitration agreement; the arbitral tribunal ordinarily determines the deeper non-signatory and jurisdictional questions under Section 16.
cases.holding: The Constitution Bench clarified the Section 11 threshold and the role of the tribunal in deciding jurisdictional questions.
cases.relevance: Directly relevant to Section 11 referral jurisdiction and non-signatory issues.

cases.name: Pravin Electricals (P) Ltd. v. Galaxy Infra & Engineering (P) Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court considered whether documentary material established an arbitration agreement at the Section 11 stage.
cases.issue: What enquiry may the referral court undertake to determine whether an arbitration agreement exists?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The referral court examines the existence of the arbitration agreement on a prima facie basis within the statutory threshold.
cases.holding: The decision illustrates the limited but necessary existence enquiry under Section 11.
cases.relevance: Direct authority on the existence-of-arbitration-agreement enquiry under Section 11.

cases.name: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
cases.facts: The Court addressed arbitrability and the extent of judicial scrutiny at the referral stage.
cases.issue: How should courts approach referral where arbitrability is disputed?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The referral court applies a prima facie standard while respecting the arbitral tribunal's jurisdiction under Section 16, subject to the statutory limits concerning non-arbitrable disputes.
cases.holding: The Court articulated the modern Indian framework governing referral and arbitrability.
cases.relevance: Relevant to the relationship between Section 11 referral and Section 16 jurisdiction.
